newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos flexes muscles to show he fit.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos flexes muscles to show he fit.

text.p: A laughing Philippine President Fidel Ramos flexed his biceps in a hospital lobby on Christmas Day to show he was back in tip-top shape after an operation to clear a major artery.
The 68-year-old former army general told reporters he would leave hospital on Thursday after one more round of blood tests and immediately return to work
"That's how you find out the level of your good cholesterol, bad cholesterol, your sugar and all the other components that go into the blood," he said.
Ramos earlier said he hoped to be home on Wednesday to spend Christmas with his grandchildren.
"The doctors asked (me) to stay one more night because we need to do a complete blood chemistry," he said after emerging from an elevator to mingle with reporters.
"But from the blood chemistry taken yesterday, it looks like we're really okay, nothing wrong, we are okay," said Ramos, dressed in a T-shirt and slacks.
"I'll be in the office at 12 noon tomorrow."

Chief heart surgeon Jorge Garcia, who removed a cholesterol blockage the size of a bean in a carotid artery that supplies blood to the brain, said Monday's 75-minute surgery was a "critical operation".
Asked if the blockage could have caused a massive stroke if it had not been cleared, Garcia said: "Absolutely. That's the reason he had surgery."
But the president was now in "good shape...(and) the artery to his brain is just as good as anyone's", Garcia said.
One of the few guests allowed into Ramos's suite was former president Corazon Aquino who advised him to take it easy.
"It's difficult here in the hospital," a presidential aide quoted Ramos as telling Aquino. "It's depressing."
Aquino gave him a get-well Christmas card and urged him to go to a convent of nuns in Manila called the "Pink Sisters" after he gets out of hospital.
"Their prayers are very powerful," Aquino, a devote Roman Catholic, told Ramos.
Ramos, a Methodist Protestant, had been known to work up to 18 hours a day prior to his illness. But he is also avid golfer and enjoys dancing.
Hospital director Raul Fores said people usually got the cholesterol-linked illness that struck Ramos "from eating too much cheese and chocolates".
